questions.question: What precision policy (number of decimal digits and rounding mode) must the high-precision internal computation apply so results are identical across systems?
questions.subject: functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: HIGH — FR-03 (Produce deterministic, high-precision results) and RSK-04 cannot be verified without a fixed precision policy; without it, the rounding differences between systems the service exists to eliminate can recur
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: a single high-precision decimal computation strategy is applied service-wide and treated as an implementation detail until stated

questions.question: What is the history retrieval contract — endpoint path, response shape, and how many recent records are returned?
questions.subject: functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: MEDIUM — FR-08 (Provide history retrieval of recent calculation records) cannot be implemented or tested without an endpoint contract
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: FR-08 is emitted with status pending and no endpoint contract; history retrieval is excluded from the MVP phase

questions.question: What numeric latency threshold should "millisecond-level response time" commit to for standard operations?
questions.subject: non_functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: HIGH — NFR-01 (performance) has no verifiable target until a number is committed; load and capacity planning for the calculate operation depend on it
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: millisecond-level interpreted as sub-second response (< 1000 ms) for standard operations

options.label: Ultra-low (< 10 ms, requires aggressive scaling budget)

questions.question: What concurrency or request-volume target must horizontal scaling support?
questions.subject: non_functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: MEDIUM — NFR-04 (Stateless design supports horizontal scaling) has no numeric capacity target, so scaling tests cannot assert pass/fail
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: horizontal scaling by adding instances with no numeric concurrency target committed

questions.question: What observability capability must be ready at launch — structured logs only, or also metrics and tracing hooks?
questions.subject: non_functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: MEDIUM — NFR-05 (Observability readiness) has no measurable target; the scope of launch-day diagnostics tooling depends on the answer
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: structured logging sufficient for diagnostics; metrics and tracing integration deferred

questions.question: What security and access-control requirements apply to the calculation API (authentication, network exposure, input limits)?
questions.subject: non_functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: HIGH — NFR-06 (Security) has no source evidence at all; the API exposure model decides whether the service is callable platform-wide or restricted
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: service treated as an internal platform component with no additional authentication assumed

options.label: Internal network, no auth (simplest, fastest adoption)
Externally reachable with full auth (highest cost)

questions.question: What usability standard should the API contract commit to, given adoption depends on simplicity?
questions.subject: non_functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: LOW — NFR-07 has no measurable usability standard; RSK-02 (teams bypassing the service) is mitigated by simplicity, so the standard affects adoption risk
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: simple payload design (operands + operation in, result out) treated as the usability baseline

questions.question: What numeric targets should replace the qualitative success criteria (teams stop duplicating math logic, results become consistent, calculations traceable)?
questions.subject: kpis
questions.why_it_matters: MEDIUM — KPI-05, KPI-06, KPI-07 are unverifiable as qualitative statements; success of the whole engagement is judged against them
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: qualitative success criteria tracked as binary (met / not met) until numeric targets are set

questions.question: Which upstream system is the first integration target for the calculate operation?
questions.subject: dependencies
questions.why_it_matters: MEDIUM — DEP-01 (Upstream consumer systems) and KPI-01 (at least one integration) need a named first consumer to sequence delivery
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: any one upstream system qualifies for the success criterion; integration sequencing left to delivery planning

questions.question: What are the budget, timeline, and staffing constraints for delivering the service?
questions.subject: constraints
questions.why_it_matters: MEDIUM — the constraints section carries pending placeholders for budget, timeline, and resource; delivery planning cannot size phases against them
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: no budget ceiling, no calendar deadline, and no staffing cap assumed; scope treated as uncapped until stated

questions.question: Are there regulatory or compliance obligations that apply to the service or its calculation records?
questions.subject: constraints
questions.why_it_matters: LOW — the regulatory constraints sub-category is a pending placeholder; if obligations exist, history retention and audit requirements in FR-06/FR-08 would change
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: no regulatory constraints assumed; history treated as diagnostic-only per the discovery transcript

questions.question: Consumer personas are technically proficient engineering roles
questions.subject: personas
questions.why_it_matters: Persona goals and pain points may not reflect actual consumer behavior, skewing API usability prioritization
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Consumer personas are technically proficient engineering roles

questions.question: The brief's conceptual API contract field names are the intended contract names
questions.subject: functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: Acceptance criteria and API documentation would use field names differing from the final implemented contract
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: The brief's conceptual API contract field names are the intended contract names

questions.question: History persistence uses a lightweight local embedded database abstraction
questions.subject: dependencies
questions.why_it_matters: Persistence design, deployment footprint, and replaceability guarantees in FR-06 would need rework
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: History persistence uses a lightweight local embedded database abstraction

questions.question: Stateless design is the mechanism that enables horizontal scaling
questions.subject: non_functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: Scaling behavior would depend on stateful components, invalidating FR-10 acceptance criteria
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Stateless design is the mechanism that enables horizontal scaling

questions.question: The reliability guarantee is stated at both FR and NFR level intentionally
questions.subject: non_functional_requirements
questions.why_it_matters: Duplicate coverage could cause inconsistent verification; if unintended, NFR-03 should be merged into FR-07
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: The reliability guarantee is stated at both FR and NFR level intentionally

questions.question: Synchronous request/response is the only interaction mode required at launch
questions.subject: scope
questions.why_it_matters: Asynchronous or batch interaction modes would require additional API surface not covered by FR-04
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Synchronous request/response is the only interaction mode required at launch

questions.question: MoSCoW priorities inferred from source phrasing (standard operations first, history optional, future capabilities planned)
questions.subject: mvp_phasing
questions.why_it_matters: Phasing would change; capabilities assumed must-have could be deferred or vice versa
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: MoSCoW priorities inferred from source phrasing (standard operations first, history optional, future capabilities planned)

questions.question: T-04 (platform service foundation) groups the stateless service shell (EPIC-07) and the API contract documentation (EPIC-08) as one foundation theme
questions.subject: theme grouping
questions.why_it_matters: Epics may be misgrouped; EPIC-08 is a documentation enabler while EPIC-07 is an infrastructure enabler, so a reviewer may prefer separate themes — grouping affects how downstream story decomposition and backlog review read the foundation layer
questions.assumption_if_unanswered: T-04 (platform service foundation) groups the stateless service shell (EPIC-07) and the API contract documentation (EPIC-08) as one foundation theme
